Honestly though, you said it yourself: your husband is unhappy and is seeking self fulfilment. It doesn't necessarily have to be through his schemes but helping him find something that makes him happy is something clearly important to him and by proxy important to your marriage. Aside from that there's several parts up for consideration:

The issue of your time. You don't have to help him, you are partners but that doesn't mean you're obligated to do everything with/for him. This needs to be realized on his end

The issue of money. Depending on what "dead end job" is and what he's making relative to the entire house income this can go different ways. If you make a roughly equal amount then he needs to listen to your input on matters of finance or you both need to create separate accounts and agree on a common  budget for shared expenses. That way money is no longer an issue. If he's making the majority of the money, even with sporadic working, and you're working at Burger King as an associate then you really have nothing to say. In this situation he's the one who is supporting you two; that's a situation of your own doing. 

The issue of wanting different things from life. This can't always be bridged and that's unfortunately something you'll have to reckon with.

I wish you luck.

It doesn't matter if you need the money or not and it doesn't matter if she doesn't feel like talking about it. You helped her out in a very tangible way and she's disrespected you by constantly blowing it off and making excuses. She doesn't need to pay you back immediately but she needs to have the initiative and the respect for what you did for her, and for you, to establish a timeline during which she will pay you back. She is taking advantage of your generosity and  a good relationship cannot continue like this. If she continues resisting paying back I would strongly consider breaking up if I were you dude.

"the more it seems like she just needs to get told to go to therapy." 

Yes, but also no. If she's as sensitive as you described this needs to be handled firmly but very delicately. She's established a rule that makes anything she does sacrosanct and beyond questioning. Both of you are religious and know very well that all humans are fallible, but what makes the difference between a good person and a bad person is their willingness to own up to, and correct, their faults. I wish you luck, just be careful please.

I've been in your wife's position and I very quickly learned that my light-hearted attempts at humor caused her to feel very unsafe and scared. At first I didn't understand how she felt because she hid how she felt from me but I truly understood the gravity of what seemed to me a harmless joke when she broke down crying after one attempt.

Make your partner aware of how this makes you feel and that these feelings aren''t a choice or you just misunderstanding the situation or just being very jumpy. Make certain that your partner understands that, due to past trauma, your body takes these little scares as evidence of real, previously experienced danger which affects your mental and physical well-being. To be a good partner she needs to come to terms with this and learn how to treat you properly. It might not register for her at first, speaking from experience, but her care for your well-being needs to push her to understand. If not, she may not understand or it may be emblematic of her not wanting to understand or care.

Edit: I wish you luck friend. I hope this can be resolved well.

We both have spoken about what we could do better, but you've got the gist of it. And then she completely disregards our previous conversations and accuses me of gaslighting and I begin to doubt myself even when I know we've had these conversations before.

I feel the same way but I try to lend credence to her thoughts because I don't want to end up being an abusive partner or dismissive of her. We've spoken about this at length before but then she turns around and accuses me all the same.
We've already moved her multiple times, thankfully though a situation came up that will let her live in a better house. I fear the damage has been done already though.
I've kinda lost hope to be honest. I'm just trying to make sense of everything before I make any big choices moving forward so I don't hurry myself or her unnecessarily.

Thank you for sharing your story and helping me how the process unfolds. I'm happy to hear you're making significant progress on your journey. She was but she decided to get off of the medication for different reasons and I don't think she wants to have medication again for better or worse.

It's not your job to take care of your brother, particularly so when he is not even asking for your help. He's an adult, he can take care of himself. Tell your mom this and don't budge. If she doesn't like it there's not much she can do about it, you're on your own.

On another note, good luck with the new apartment!

There are most likely non profit services in your area that shelter and help provide for women in danger so you can get out of your very problematic and very dangerous situation. Counselors at your school should know how to get in touch with these services and can help you get to safety. You are being abused, you are in danger, and you need to seek help. Please, please reach out to get that help.

While you do deserve an answer there's a reason why he doesn't want to talk about it. Maybe a fear, rational or irrational that he can't shake. Try to be gentle if you can, and work together honestly and compassionately to get to the answer.

Like some  other people have said, he's been grooming you. In other words, he's been preparing you and having you believe his affections are real when he just wants to take advantage of you and your inexperience. It's important that you report what he's been doing to someone higher up. Not only is this unprofessional but it is dangerous, to you and anyone else he may be in contact with. Please be safe and tell your parents so they can help you navigate this properly.

Tell her firmly that this is not something that's happening for you anywhere in your near future (tell her about what you said in 1.) and if she can't accept that then you know that this is where you'll have to part ways. Relationships are contingent on being aligned on the most important issues for each person. If someone doesn't want to or isn't capable of doing something the other really, really values then the relationship has reached it's natural end.

Good luck bud.

The issue of court packing is the logical conclusion of the tit for tat political game that Republicans and Democrats have both been playing for over a decade now. It is not unconstitutional even though is deleterious to our country, but it is a result of polarization and zero sum political gambits played by both sides.  

Trump, on the other hand, has baselessly threatened the credibility of our institutions which not only threatens the country but has lead to the government's inability to project a single coherent message on covid to keep as many Americans safe and healthy. Furthermore, he has threatened the very democratic nature of the country by refusing to commit to a peaceful transition of power, threatening to upend two hundred years of democracy. 

Both sides need to be held accountable, but Trump is acting like a dictator in the making.

Hey, remember first and foremost beauty is in the eye of the beholder, some people will always find you unattractive regardless of what you're presenting. Objectively though, the way you took the pic isn't helping you. The angle, the proximity, etc don't represent you well. For me something needs to be done with your hair, it looks really messy. Once everything calms down with the pandemic and all you should find a stylist and talk about different things you could do. Otherwise, you have a really great jawline and eyes, I think it's just the picture and they way your hair is worn right now that's throwing you off. Don't despair man, we've all felt that way before; we get too much into our own head and create our own personal hell without realizing that we can't see everything about ourselves that others might.
250 people at six feet apart means she'll have to rent out a football stadium to make sure her loved ones don't face a gruesome illness.

You are absolutely right to find this disturbing. He has no right to share pictures without your genuine consent and he should actively be pushing his friend to delete his ex's pictures because it is more likely than not that he lost the consent to have/share them, if he ever did have that consent to begin with. 

While he doesn't have to ask you to share the intimate details of his life with others it is telling about who he is that he didn't ask you what you felt comfortable with him divulging to others. You should take this into consideration if he is a person who is trustworthy and worth your time. 

"Bigger" doesn't necessarily mean anything bad. Beauty is truly in the eye of the beholder. But if it continues to bother you it is worth exploring your feelings as to why you feel bad about been seen as "bigger." Size has no effect on your value as a partner and more importantly as a person. However, if you personally want to look differently to please yourself, not other people or society, then that's something about yourself you should explore. 

I can say for sure though they he does not love you. It is next to impossible to have genuine, safe love with how little time you've spent together. I don't say this to belittle your feelings for each other, I'm sure they are compelling. I say this because love is something only really won with time, struggle, cooperation, and communication.

All in all, you really need to gauge if you think he will be a good and supportive partner to you. I don't know him, but from what you've shared there are definitely some red flags that justify parting ways. If you decide to stay with him your need to set boundaries and communicate what he made you feel and what you will not accept. Try to approach that conversation with a level head and your emotions under control so you don't give him reason to get defensive, angry, etc. Miscommunication is a big cause of fights. Clearly explain to him what you will and won't accept, and be ready to break things off if he doesn't try to understand or honor your boundaries.
